scope.summary: Author the UserManual BodyKit chapter per Section 13.27 (HBR-MAN + CX-982): purpose, channel workflow including decoupling and over-range, genital configuration in direct language, export profiles and round-trip, recipe save/share, all 8 MCP tools with exact wire names and examples, failure modes with recovery, and the diagnostics posture — sufficient for a no-context model to operate BodyKit end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: The chapter seeds into the UserManual store covering: BodyKit purpose and architecture summary; the channel workflow (region groups, decoupling guarantee, designed over-range, coupling links and isolation); genital configuration documented in direct production language; export profiles with unit/axis contracts and the FBX-via-Blender-bridge rule; recipes incl. PNG share cards; and the archetype QA surface.

All 8 MCP tools are documented with their EXACT wire names (author_body, edit_body, get_body, solve_measurements, randomize_body, pose_body, configure_genitals, export_body), input/output schemas, and one worked example each.
Common failure modes and recovery steps are documented (decouple violation -> suggested_fix loop, stale proxies, bridge-missing-Blender, license-guard rejection, infeasible measurement targets).
The diagnostics posture section records the HBR-INT-009 tier states (FlightRecorder WIRED, internal_diagnostics/Palmistry DEFERRED with reasons) for BodyKit surfaces.
The manual self-consistency test passes, and the no-context operation test drives one documented flow (author -> edit -> export) using only chapter content.
scope.risk_if_missed: Every fresh model session re-derives BodyKit's workflow from source code — slow, error-prone, and in direct violation of the built-in-manual requirement the project treats as a first-class product surface.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
